$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Every fact here is read from Google's own discovery document (https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v1beta), not from docs prose.
title: Google Analytics

oauth.$scopeComment: analytics.readonly, not analytics. The discovery document lists both for runReport and this action only READS -- granting write access to run a report would let an automation modify property configuration it never needs to touch.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. Google's access tokens last ONE HOUR, so refreshToken is required rather than optional.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. Analytics has no test estate -- there is one API and a property is a real property. This action only reads, so the blast radius is a quota charge rather than a change, but it is still real data.
sandboxNote: Google Analytics has no sandbox. A report reads a real property's real data and spends real quota. The faker returns a plausibly-shaped report so a flow can be built without a Google account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials. ONE value for the whole installation, not per connected account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: The client secret for the same OAuth app. One value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account, and it expires after ONE HOUR. The host refreshes it with the refresh token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Google account. Google issues one only when the consent request asks for offline access.
